subject: Business
title: Equity Splits and Vesting
description: A fast breakdown of Equity Splits and Vesting for builders.

hook.text: Two co-founders split equity 50/50 on day one. One quits at month six. Half the company walks out.

buildup.text: Vesting releases equity over time — typically four years with a one-year cliff.

discovery.text: The cliff means leaving before year one gets you nothing. It prevents free-riding.

twist.text: Equal splits feel fair but ignore reality. Contributions are never truly equal over four years.

climax.text: Y Combinator advises: split based on expected contribution and use standard four-year vesting.

punchline.text: Equity is earned over time, not gifted at the start.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a vesting cliff?
options: To prevent someone from leaving early with a large equity stake
To delay all equity until the company goes public
To give founders more control over investors

details.summary: Equity splits divide ownership among founders, employees, and investors, while vesting schedules ensure equity is earned over time. Standard startup vesting is four years with a one-year cliff, protecting the company if someone leaves early while rewarding those who stay and contribute.
details.whyItMatters: Equity decisions made at founding have permanent consequences. Poor splits breed resentment and motivate departures. Missing vesting schedules let departed founders keep windfalls.
takeaways: Equity splits should reflect contribution, commitment, and future value creation
Four-year vesting with a one-year cliff is the standard startup equity schedule
Vesting protects against co-founders who leave early with unearned equity stakes

faq.question: What is a one-year cliff in vesting?
faq.answer: The cliff means no equity vests until the first anniversary. If someone leaves before one year, they get nothing. After the cliff, equity typically vests monthly over the remaining three years. This protects the company from giving permanent ownership to someone who contributes only briefly.

faq.question: Should co-founders always split equity equally?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Equal splits are simple but may not reflect reality. Consider who originated the idea, who brings more relevant expertise, who invests more time, and who takes more financial risk. Have the conversation openly and early.
